brief: October saw equity indices broadly resilient, with most MSCI World sectors up, while a severe sector rotation hit technology. The S&P 500 fell 0.9% in October as its six largest members averaged a 7.1% drop, while the equal-weighted index rose 4.9% and the semiconductor index (SOX) fell 15.4%, down 25% since June. Still-firm US inflation revived rate-hike expectations, adding pressure. The Democrats' midterm win lifted equities initially, then reversed sharply on November 5 on fears it would slow US data center buildout, hitting the whole AI value chain. The speed of the move suggests forced hedge fund deleveraging, with rising stock correlations and momentum-strategy underperformance. Short-term deleveraging risk remains substantial given hard-to-measure residual leverage, but Edmond de Rothschild sees AI fundamentals as sound medium-term, citing historical post-selloff Nasdaq rebounds and low credit spreads (340bps). Its models show first-tier AI valuations already pricing in a 30-80% 2030 capex cut, versus 15-30% for second-tier names, which it judges too pessimistic. Consensus has the five hyperscalers' capex rising from $379bn in 2025 to $1,345bn in 2030. Other drivers named: Nvidia's CEO resigning after affair revelations, hot CPI and PPI data, and CoreWeave's reassuring results, which erased most of the November 5 Nasdaq drop.
